mechanism: Relaxes blood vessels so blood flows more easily.
serious_warnings: Prescription only.
Do not stop suddenly without medical advice.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General management of high blood pressure and chest pain (as prescribed).

mechanism: Interferes with bacterial cell-wall formation, killing susceptible bacteria.
precautions: Tell your doctor about any penicillin allergy
serious_warnings: Do not use without a prescription.
Can cause serious allergic reactions in penicillin-allergic people.
Antibiotic misuse drives resistance; complete only the course a doctor prescribes.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: Treatment of certain bacterial infections (as prescribed by a doctor).

mechanism: Stops bacteria from making proteins they need to grow.
precautions: Tell your doctor about heart-rhythm problems
serious_warnings: Prescription only; do not self-medicate.
Can affect heart rhythm in some people.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: Treatment of certain bacterial respiratory and other infections (doctor prescribed).

mechanism: Blocks histamine H1 receptors to reduce allergic symptoms.
serious_warnings: May impair alertness in sensitive people.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General relief of allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and itching.

mechanism: Blocks dopamine receptors to reduce nausea and improve gut movement.
serious_warnings: Can affect heart rhythm; use lowest dose for shortest time.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General relief of nausea, vomiting, and bloating (short-term, as advised).

mechanism: Reduces prostaglandins by inhibiting COX enzymes, lowering inflammation and pain.
precautions: Caution in ulcers, kidney or heart disease
serious_warnings: May cause stomach bleeding or ulcers, especially with long-term use.
Can affect kidney function and blood pressure.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General relief of pain, inflammation, and fever.

mechanism: Selectively blocks peripheral histamine H1 receptors.
serious_warnings: Rare allergic reactions.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General relief of allergy symptoms with low drowsiness.

mechanism: Lowers glucose production by the liver and improves insulin sensitivity.
serious_warnings: Prescription only.
Rare but serious lactic acidosis, especially with kidney problems.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General management of type 2 diabetes (as prescribed by a doctor).

mechanism: Reduces stomach acid production by blocking the acid pump in stomach cells.
precautions: Discuss long-term use with a doctor
serious_warnings: Long-term use may affect magnesium, vitamin B12, and bone health.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General management of acidity, heartburn, and acid-related stomach problems.

mechanism: Provides balanced glucose and electrolytes to help the gut absorb water.
precautions: Prepare with clean water exactly as directed on the sachet
serious_warnings: Seek urgent care if there is blood in stool, no urine, or persistent vomiting.
side_effects: Mild vomiting if taken too fast
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: Prevention and correction of dehydration from diarrhea or vomiting.

mechanism: Believed to act centrally to reduce fever and the perception of pain.
serious_warnings: Overdose can cause severe liver damage.
Do not combine multiple products containing paracetamol.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General relief of mild-to-moderate pain and reduction of fever.

mechanism: Relaxes airway muscles to open the airways.
serious_warnings: Prescription guidance recommended.
Frequent need may signal poorly controlled asthma - see a doctor.
source: General public reference (standard formulary / WHO educational information)
uses: General relief of breathing difficulty and wheezing (as prescribed).
